ai_show_review.summary: Brief high‑quality instrumental tease, not a full Dead set
ai_show_review.blurb: The only surviving tape is a ~5‑minute soundboard instrumental jam. The audio is crisp and clean, but none of the two‑song set (Viola Lee Blues, Alice D. Millionaire) is captured.
ai_show_review.review: On Halloween night 1966 at California Hall the Dead took the stage with Jerry, Bob, Phil, Bill Kreutzmann and Pigpen. Unfortunately the sole surviving recording – a soundboard capture identified as gd1966-10-31.sbd.bershaw.5416.shnf – contains only a short instrumental tease that lasts about five minutes and does not feature any of the scheduled songs. While the fidelity is excellent (“5‑star sound” according to reviewers), listeners won’t hear the band’s early blues‑rock set or Pigpen’s harmonica. For completists who want any glimpse of the group’s 1966 studio vibe, this tape is a clean snapshot; otherwise it offers little insight into the actual concert.

best_recording.reason: Only available recording; soundboard quality is excellent despite being just a brief instrumental jam and not the full show.

key_highlights: Crisp, clean soundboard capture of a short instrumental tease
No full set captured – only ~5 minutes of music
